blocks.text: "ESTABLISHED TO BE A PROPHET OF THE LORD" (1 SAMUEL 3:20); ALSO "THE SEER" (1 SAMUEL 9:19) · THE JUDGES
Samuel. Called by name in the night at Shiloh; the LORD let none of his words fall to the ground.
1 Samuel 3 · Called by name at Shiloh
1 SAMUEL 3 · CALLED BY NAME AT SHILOH
“And the LORD came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth.”

Before the call, "Samuel did not yet know the LORD, neither was the word of the LORD yet revealed unto him". Afterwards "the LORD revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of the LORD. And the word of Samuel came to all Israel." 1 Samuel 3:7 1 Samuel 3:21–4:1

"The LORD had told Samuel in his ear a day before Saul came"; "Then came the word of the LORD unto Samuel"; at Jesse’s house the LORD named which son to anoint. 1 Samuel 9:15–17 1 Samuel 15:10 1 Samuel 16:6–12
He was called "the seer": "he that is now called a Prophet was beforetime called a Seer". Saul’s servant said of him that everything he says comes to pass. 1 Samuel 9:6 1 Samuel 9:9 1 Samuel 9:19

He prayed for the people: he "cried unto the LORD for Israel; and the LORD heard him", and promised, "God forbid that I should sin against the LORD in ceasing to pray for you". 1 Samuel 7:9 1 Samuel 12:23
At Naioth in Ramah "the company of the prophets" prophesied with "Samuel standing as appointed over them". 1 Samuel 19:20

He wrote: "Samuel told the people the manner of the kingdom, and wrote it in a book, and laid it up before the LORD." Chronicles cites "the book of Samuel the seer" for the acts of David. 1 Samuel 10:25 1 Chronicles 29:29
“It is the LORD: let him do what seemeth him good.”
“Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.”
KING OF JUDAH, THEN OF ALL ISRAEL
“Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of the LORD came upon David from that day forward.”
“As thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women.”
The word in its main themes
Return to the LORD with all your hearts
“If ye do return unto the LORD with all your hearts, then put away the strange gods and Ashtaroth from among you, and prepare your hearts unto the LORD, and serve him only”
“And ye shall cry out in that day because of your king which ye shall have chosen you; and the LORD will not hear you in that day.”
Fear the LORD and serve him
“Only fear the LORD, and serve him in truth with all your heart: for consider how great things he hath done for you.”
To obey is better than sacrifice
“For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. Because thou hast rejected the word of the LORD, he hath also rejected thee from being king.”
“for the Lord seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.”
To whom the word was spoken
“Gather all Israel to Mizpeh, and I will pray for you unto the LORD.”
“I will call unto the LORD, and he shall send thunder and rain; that ye may perceive and see that your wickedness is great”
“But now thy kingdom shall not continue: the LORD hath sought him a man after his own heart”
“The LORD hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou.”
“to morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me”
Thunder and rain at wheat harvest
Oil and three signs for Saul
Who stood with him, and against him
"And Samuel died; and all the Israelites were gathered together, and lamented him, and buried him in his house at Ramah." 1 Samuel 25:1

1 Samuel 28 tells of the woman at Endor bringing up one whom Saul "perceived" to be Samuel, who told him that Israel would be delivered to the Philistines and "to morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me"; Chronicles says Saul died for "asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit". 1 Samuel 28:3–20 1 Chronicles 10:13–14

Later Scripture sets him beside Moses: "Moses and Aaron among his priests, and Samuel among them that call upon his name"; "Though Moses and Samuel stood before me". Peter counts "all the prophets from Samuel"; Paul says God gave judges "until Samuel the prophet". Psalms 99:6 Jeremiah 15:1 Acts 3:24 Acts 13:20

Jerome, writing in his own day, asks whether "the Emperor Arcadius" was guilty of sacrilege, "who after so long a time has conveyed the bones of the blessed Samuel from Judea to Thrace", with crowds meeting the relics "from Palestine to Chalcedon".[29] Who says so: Jerome, Against Vigilantius 5, about AD 406
Tertullian (about AD 200); followed by Jerome, Luther and Calvin, as reported by Kirkpatrick (1884)

Tertullian writes that the spirit consulted at Endor was "permitted ... to represent the soul of Samuel", and "God forbid, however, that we should suppose that the soul of any saint, much less of a prophet, can be dragged out of (its resting-place in Hades) by a demon."[28]
"A modern hypothesis", as reported by Kirkpatrick (1884)
Kirkpatrick reports a view that the woman, in a trance, imagined she saw and heard Samuel. He answers that the dialogue runs "directly" between Saul and Samuel.[25]
A deliberate deception by the woman
Kirkpatrick reports a view that the woman pretended to see Samuel and used her own voice or a confederate’s. He says it "finds no support in the narrative".[25]

Scripture gives no age for Samuel at his call.
1 Samuel 28:19 says "to morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me", and 1 Samuel 31:6 tells of Saul’s death with three sons; the text does not say there that the word came to pass.
The book named after Samuel does not say who wrote it; Scripture names one writing of his (1 Samuel 10:25) and "the book of Samuel the seer" (1 Chronicles 29:29).
